messages:
maya (eng-platform): FYI the new client auto-batching patch in TS/Py SDKs reduces requests but changes token accounting per-request. Console quota charts spike unpredictably for some tenants during tests.
josh (eng): what's the change exactly?
priya (devex): SDK now bundles small prompt calls into a single upstream request by default (window=10ms). That saves tokens on net, but our quota meter counts upstream requests *and* then attributes tokens to the first route header seen. When multiple logical routes are batched the attribution is wrong.
tom (eng-ml): Oof. So multiple features sharing a client could have their quota burn show up under one route and others look zero?
claire (ux): Yep — we saw an internal demo where the A/B test route disappeared from the tile. Very confusing for product teams.
josh (eng): Root cause: batch request merges payloads; the SDK sends a single composite payload with per-item metadata, but the server-side meter only reads the top-level route header.
priya (devex): Proposed fixes: a) SDK expands outgoing header to include per-item route metadata in a metadata array and server attributes per-output; b) server-side batching-aware attribution that splits tokens across per-item route fields; c) SDK disables auto-batching by default and makes it opt-in.
maya (eng-platform): We can't disable batching by default — performance win is big for small bursty workloads. We need accurate console attribution.
josh (eng): I can add a lightweight per-item metadata envelope in the batch request:
```
{
  batch: [
    {route: "feature-A", prompt: "..."},
    {route: "feature-B", prompt: "..."}
  ]
}
```
Then server can read batch[*].route and split cost. Minimal change.
tom (eng-ml): Also need token-splitting logic: how do we apportion generated tokens if model returns a single concatenated stream? We should have model produce per-item outputs. The runtime already supports per-item generation in the batch path.
claire (ux): From dashboard side, we just need consistent keys and per-feature burn numbers. If server emits per-item metrics we can surface them as separate series.
priya (devex): Migration plan idea: 1) SDK ships batched envelope with per-item route metadata (backward compatible: also include legacy top-level route header for single-item requests); 2) server updates meter to prefer per-item fields when present, else fallback to header; 3) console ingestion accepts both and dedups by request id. Canary for 48h.
josh (eng): Implementation note: keep the envelope field name `items` to avoid collision. Example JS snippet: 
```js
client.batch([{
  route: 'feature-A',
  input: '...'
}, {
  route: 'feature-B',
  input: '...'
}])
```
priya (devex): For Py docs I'll show opt-out flag for customers who rely on old attribution while they test: `Client(auto_batching=True, batching_route_headers='legacy_compat')`
maya (eng-platform): Important: telemetry sampling happens before attribution in some paths. Ensure attribution runs before sampling decision.
josh (eng): noted — I'll reorder sampling hook. Add unit tests to verify per-item metrics emitted.
tom (eng-ml): Also add a fallback heuristic: if per-item outputs missing, attribute proportionally by input token length. Not perfect but better than all-to-one.
claire (ux): Can we tag the console series as "inferred attribution" during canary so users know values might be approximate?
priya (devex): Yes — console can show a small badge during migration.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary for batching-attribution on Wed 02:00 UTC, 48h window, 5/25/50/80 ramp. Link: https://deploys/redwood/canary/5088
maya (eng-platform): Action items: @josh add per-item envelope + tests (EOD Thu), @priya update SDK docs + example flags (EOD Wed), @claire add UX badge + instrumentation check (Mon), @tom add proportional fallback logic (Fri).
priya (devex): I'll also carve out a short announcement script for #announcements and include a troubleshooting snippet for customers seeing weird quota numbers.
maya (eng-platform): If after 14 days metrics look stable we'll keep envelope as permanent API. If not, revert to header-only and re-evaluate.
josh (eng): I'll open the PR and mark it migration:batch-attr.
claire (ux): thanks all — want minimal user surprise.
priya (devex): I'll coordinate support playbook with CS.
